trials.hypothesis: This keeps the baseline body and replaces the 1x1 placement head. For each brick type, it max-pools and min-pools the body features over that type's footprint window, then scores the result with a small per-type MLP. That gives the head an AND/MAX over the footprint cells, which matches how the landing layer is set and when a placement is correct. Refuted if dev success is no better than the baseline beyond seed noise.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
HID = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * WIDTH, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            if dy == 1 and dx == 1:
                mx = f
                mn = f
            else:
                p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob2(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 24
HID = 16
GW = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        c_in = 4 + 3 + 1
        self.c1 = nn.Conv3d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv3d(2 * WIDTH, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv3d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        if self.Z > 1:
            zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, self.Z)
        else:
            zc = torch.zeros(1)
        self.register_buffer('zc', zc)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = self.zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, planes, zc], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.c1(x))
        f = f + F.relu(self.c2(f))
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            if dy == 1 and dx == 1:
                mx = f
                mn = f
            else:
                p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool3d(p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool3d(-p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            s = head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1))
            outs.append(s.amax(dim=2))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3, 4)), f.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HEADS = 4


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, spec.Y * spec.X, WIDTH) * 0.02)
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(WIDTH, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(WIDTH, 2 * WIDTH), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH))
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        B, W, Y, X = f.shape
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        h = self.ln1(t)
        a, _ = self.attn(h, h, h, need_weights=False)
        t = t + a
        t = t + self.mlp(self.ln2(t))
        f2 = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, W, Y, X)
        place = self.place_head(f2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f2.mean((2, 3)), f2.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
PROJ = 32
HID = 16


def fp_pool(h, dy, dx):
    if dy == 1 and dx == 1:
        return h, h
    p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return mx, mn


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * PROJ, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        h = F.relu(f + self.ctx(g)[:, :, None, None])
        q = F.relu(self.proj(h))
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            mx, mn = fp_pool(q, fp[0], fp[1])
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 40
GW = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 16

    if dy == 1 and dx == 1:
        return h, h
    p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)

        self.r2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)

        q = F.relu(self.proj(f))

            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))

        g = self.glob2(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
GW = 64
D = 24
HID = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        Z = self.Z
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(GW, D)
        self.cproj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, D, 1)
        self.lay1 = nn.Conv3d(4 + 3 + Z + 1, D, 1)
        self.lay2 = nn.Conv3d(D, D, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv3d(2 * D, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv3d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.place2d = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        if Z > 1:
            zlin = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z)
        else:
            zlin = torch.zeros(1)
        zc = torch.cat([torch.eye(Z), zlin.view(1, Z)], dim=0)
        self.register_buffer('zc', zc)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = self.zc.view(1, Z + 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z + 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, planes, zc], dim=1)
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        c2 = self.cproj(f) + self.ctx(g)[:, :, None, None]
        u = F.relu(self.lay1(x) + c2.unsqueeze(2))
        u = F.relu(self.lay2(u))
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            if dy == 1 and dx == 1:
                mx = u
                mn = u
            else:
                p = F.pad(u, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool3d(p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool3d(-p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            s = head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1))
            outs.append(torch.logsumexp(s, dim=2))
        place = (torch.cat(outs, dim=1) + self.place2d(f)).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())

        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * PROJ, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        h = F.relu(f + self.ctx(g)[:, :, None, None])

            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, so these choices come from the task's structure. A brick lands on the highest filled cell under its footprint. A placement is correct only if every footprint cell is missing at that same landing layer and no needed cell gets sealed underneath it. The baseline scores every brick type from the features of the anchor cell alone, through a 1x1 conv. That means the per-type comparison across the footprint has to be squeezed into the body's features. The baseline also has no way to let global state (progress, which layers are done) shape the per-cell placement logits. So round 1 tests two single changes against the baseline: (1) a footprint-pooled, type-specific head and (2) global context broadcast back to every cell. The third candidate combines both with a residual body at about the baseline's compute. Every candidate stays close to 1x the baseline's training compute, because 131k steps is only 128 PPO updates.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that all three round-1 files trained without errors at 1.0 to 1.35 times the starting compute. None of the round-1 ideas can be ranked yet: footprint pooling, global context and the residual combination. The final selection keeps the top 3 dev scores, so this round should spread its bets while each design stays easy to read. The task depends on per-layer logic. A brick lands at the highest build cell under its footprint, and it is correct only if the target has missing cells across that whole footprint at that layer. A 2D conv sees layers only as stacked channels. Round 2 therefore tests: (1) a 3D voxel encoder whose footprint head scores each layer and takes the maximum over layers; (2) global self-attention after the conv body, so placement order can depend on the whole grid; (3) the two cleanest round-1 single changes, footprint head plus context broadcast, combined at baseline width. All three stay under 1.7 times the starting compute.
analyses.3: No scores are visible, so the six trials cannot be ranked. All of them trained without errors. The final choice will be made on dev scores, so the remaining trials should go to the ideas most likely to win. Every candidate so far that added a footprint head or attention cost 1.3–2.4× the starting compute, so it trained for only 54k–99k of the 131k steps. On a sparse-success task the lost steps may cost more than the inductive bias gains. Two of this round's candidates keep the ideas I think are strongest: max/min pooling over each brick's footprint, which matches the landing rule, and a broadcast global context, which helps with build order. Both stay at about 1.1× compute so they get nearly the full budget. One varies only the head's cost; the other uses a deeper body that sees the whole grid. The third tests a new idea: a cheap per-layer head built from 1×1 layers that scores each placement at each layer, rather than repeating the costly 3D convs of r2c1.
analyses.4: No success scores are visible, so this round can't rank the trials. All 9 trials trained without errors. Two earlier choices look sound for reasons that don't depend on scores. A footprint-pooled per-type head matches how a brick lands and when a placement is correct. Keeping compute near 1.0x keeps training steps close to the full 131k, which matters because seed luck is large and fewer steps hurt PPO. The 3D bodies, attention and wider heads cost 1.3-2.4x, which means fewer training steps. The cheap context + footprint head in r3c1 (1.13x) is the most efficient design in this family. With one round left, I refine r3c1 at about 1.1-1.2x compute. One candidate adds a third conv layer so each cell sees a 7x7 neighbourhood. One adds a learned 1x1 skip from the raw cell observation into the head, so it gets exact column and target detail without the body blurring it. The third combines both, giving the two changes a chance to add up.
